card: PR 36042 raises the minimum supported GCC version from 12.1 to 13.1 and enforces `<format>` support during CMake configuration. This allows Bitcoin Core to adopt C++20 std::format in place of tinyformat and paves the way for C++23 support. CI environments are updated to match, including upgrading the previous-releases container to Ubuntu 24.04 and NetBSD cross-builds to libstdc++-14. Developers building with GCC on older distributions without modern toolchain packages will need to use Clang or newer GCC toolsets.
changed_since_previous: Cleaned up obsolete GCC 13 notes in Windows build documentation, removed redundant manual `-Werror` flags in the native previous-releases CI script, and tweaked NetBSD cross-compilation configuration.
evidence: PR description: "(For this bump, only C++20 std::format will become available, but this bump should also pave the way for C++23.) This patch will only be released in version 33.x, or later, next year (2027)."
Issue #34979 is linked as discussing when it is acceptable to drop support for older vanilla operating systems lacking GCC 13.
problem: Bitcoin Core cannot use C++20 `std::format` across all supported toolchains because GCC 12 lacks implementation, forcing continued reliance on `tinyformat` / `strprintf` and delaying readiness for C++23.

risk.why: Compiler baseline changes affect toolchain compatibility across supported distribution environments and can break builds on older developer systems or CI targets.

scope_notes: Touches CI environment setup scripts for Ubuntu and NetBSD cross-compilation to provide GCC 13/14 runtime and headers.
summary: Bumps the minimum supported GCC version from 12.1 to 13.1 and adds a CMake configure-time check requiring C++20 `<format>` support. Updates CI test environments to GCC 13+ (upgrading the native previous releases runner to Ubuntu 24.04 and NetBSD cross-compilation to libstdc++-14), and converts a benchmark from `tinyformat` to `std::format` as an example.
